//: Canonical destructive-command rule table for both cluster repos. This file is the single source of truth: .claude/hooks/guard-destructive.sh and .opencode/plugins/guard-destructive.js are GENERATED from it by gen-guards.py, so the bash and JS guards cannot drift apart. Patterns are written in the intersection of POSIX ERE (grep -E) and JavaScript RegExp so one string serves both.

always_allow.//: Read-only validation is never blocked, whatever else the command matches.

rules.reason: A subagent may not mutate the live cluster — these commands are the human's to run. The safety of 'mise run //kube/clusters/artemis:apply-ks' is not in the task, it is in the procedure around it: suspend root + target first, watch the result, wait for confirmation, resume in order after CI is green. A subagent skips all four.
rules.alternative: Write the manifests and validate them offline ('mise run //kube/clusters/artemis:render-ks <ns> <ks>' needs no cluster), or read live state with 'mise run //kube/clusters/artemis:diff-ks <ns> <ks>'. Report the change and let the human apply it.

rules.reason: A subagent may not mutate the live cluster — these commands are the human's to run. The safety of 'just kube apply-ks' is not in the recipe, it is in the procedure around it: suspend root + target first, watch the result, wait for confirmation, resume in order after CI is green. A subagent skips all four.
rules.alternative: Write the manifests and validate them offline ('just kube render-local-ks <ns> <ks>' needs no cluster), or read live state with 'kubectl get <kind> -n <ns> <name> --context frostlink'. Report the change and let the human apply it.

rules.reason: A subagent may not mutate a live cluster — these tasks are the human's to run. The safety of 'mise run //kube/clusters/<cluster>:apply-ks' is not in the task, it is in the procedure around it: suspend root + target first, watch the result, wait for confirmation, resume in order after CI is green. A subagent skips all four.
rules.alternative: Write the manifests and validate them offline ('mise run //kube/clusters/<cluster>:render-ks <ns> <ks>' needs no cluster), or read live state with 'mise run //kube/clusters/<cluster>:diff-ks <ns> <ks>'. On Frostlink read with 'kubectl get <kind> -n <ns> <name> --context frostlink'. Report the change and let the human apply it.

rules.reason: A subagent may not write to git history — staging, committing, pushing, rebasing and merging are the human's. Agent definitions that promise 'never writes' are frontmatter, which is cached at session start and cannot be relied on; this rule is a PreToolUse hook, so it holds under every permission mode including --dangerously-skip-permissions.
rules.alternative: Leave the working tree dirty and report what you changed. The human stages by name, runs 'git diff --staged', and commits. Read-only git (status, log, diff, show, worktree) is unaffected.
Apply through the apply-ks task of the cluster: 'mise run //kube/clusters/<cluster>:apply-ks <ns> <ks>' (standalone frostlink repo: 'just kube apply-ks <ns> <ks>')

rules.exempt_reason: PVC recreation (miroir StorageClass migrations, restore drills) is routine and always paired with a verified kopiur snapshot. The marker opts a single command out of THIS rule only -- every other rule, including talosctl reset/wipe, still applies. Runbook: .agents/skills/recreate-pvc (Artemis). Frostlink restores go through 'mise run //kube/clusters/frostlink:restore-pvc' (kopiur-restore skill) and need no marker.
rules.alternative: Confirm with the user before deleting cluster resources. If this is a planned PVC recreation with a verified snapshot, append the marker documented in .agents/skills/recreate-pvc (Artemis); on Frostlink use 'mise run //kube/clusters/frostlink:restore-pvc' instead

rules.reason: Direct helm mutations are not allowed — config lives in HelmRelease manifests
rules.alternative: Edit the HelmRelease values and apply via Flux
Confirm with the user before deleting Flux resources

rules.reason: talosctl patch machineconfig duplicates array fields (machine.files etc.) and can brick the node
rules.alternative: Use 'mise run //kube/clusters/artemis/talos:apply-node <node>' or talosctl apply-config --file for full config replacement

rules.reason: talosctl patch machineconfig duplicates array fields (machine.files etc.) and can brick the node
rules.alternative: Use a minimal DELTA patch file, or 'talosctl apply-config --file' for a full replacement — never pass talos/patches/controlplane.yaml, it is a gen-time patch and will strand the node

rules.reason: talosctl patch machineconfig duplicates array fields (machine.files etc.) and can brick the node
rules.alternative: Artemis: 'mise run //kube/clusters/artemis/talos:apply-node <node>' or talosctl apply-config --file for full config replacement. Frostlink: a minimal DELTA patch file, or 'talosctl apply-config --file' — never pass kube/clusters/frostlink/talos/patches/controlplane.yaml, it is a gen-time patch and will strand the node

rules.reason: talosctl reset/wipe is destructive and irreversible
rules.alternative: Confirm explicitly with the user before proceeding

rules.reason: Frostlink is a single node — talosctl upgrade/reboot/shutdown is a FULL cluster outage with nothing to fail over to
rules.alternative: Use 'just talos upgrade <version>' (it resolves the schematic first), and only with the user watching

rules.exempt_reason: A bare talosctl call cannot say which cluster it targets, so it is treated as Frostlink unless the command names Artemis (a talosconfig path or context containing 'artemis'). The mise tasks run talosctl inside the task, so this rule never sees them.
rules.reason: Frostlink is a single node — talosctl upgrade/reboot/shutdown is a FULL cluster outage with nothing to fail over to. This command does not name Artemis, so it may target Frostlink
rules.alternative: Frostlink: 'mise run //kube/clusters/frostlink/talos:upgrade <version>' (it resolves the schematic first), and only with the user watching. Artemis: 'mise run //kube/clusters/artemis/talos:upgrade-node <node>', or name Artemis in the command (--context artemis or its talosconfig)

rules.reason: Recursive delete on a sensitive path
rules.alternative: Confirm the exact path with the user before deleting

rules.reason: mv REPLACES a mise-managed symlink with a regular file, silently unlinking it from ~/dotfiles — edits then stop reaching the repo
rules.alternative: Use `cp` instead of `mv`, which writes through the symlink and keeps it intact
